title: Homes that don't claim, and shared field ground
why: Open 0, New 1, Miss 1, Reach 2. The rules are settled in the brief down to the harvest's reap-share-take order, and done is exact: every map's scores equal to the base's, and the tests it writes on a staged shared home. Adapted from the claim, sow and harvest code there is. It reaches every turn: the move and harvest steps, reap, in_reach. A slip in who gathers shows as a score that differs from the base on the retro maps, so the checks and its own sweep catch it. About 13 files, 500 lines new and 200 moved: dividing.rs (~200 moved out of clans.rs, 621 lines), homes.rs (~80), clans.rs (~70), fields.rs (~50), markets.rs, stats.rs, data.rs, world.rs, web/src/lib.rs, core/tests/towns.rs (~250), cli/tests/save.rs pins, engine/CLAUDE.md, homes.md.

title: A turn that scales
why: Open 2, New 1, Miss 0, Reach 2. Four refactors, each digest-safe, so build-1's pins and the digests catch any slip. Done is in part a search for speed: at most 0.35 of main's ms a turn, which the spec step reached with the scouts' bound (given as a diff) and a crude search exit. The exit has to bound by the cheapest step, which the brief says and probe.md shows. Adapted from cost_map_by and path_by. It reaches every turn's go, trade and people steps. About 8 files, 300 lines: markets.rs (~80), land.rs or reach.rs (~80), scout.rs (~10), ai.rs (~20), world.rs (the per-turn cache), web/src/lib.rs, core/tests/towns.rs (~80), scale.md.

title: The town, the judge and the page
why: Open 2, New 1, Miss 1, Reach 1. The reading, the event, every count, the seventh run, the panels and the script are named in the brief, after judge_fields.rs, sweep_fields.rs and fields.mjs. How the cluster of hearths and the town mark read at a glance is judged by eye from towns.png (Open 2). Its own tests and towns.mjs catch a missing count or mark. It reaches the markets step's end, the judge and the sweep, not the rules. Large but patterned: about 20 files, 800 lines new and about 450 moved: towns.rs (~80), judge_towns.rs (~200), judge_scores.rs (~220 moved out of judge.rs, 641 lines), sweep_towns.rs (~200), sweep_total.rs (~230 moved out of sweep_judge.rs, 599), sweep_judge.rs, sweep_text.rs, data.rs, events.rs, markets.rs, web/src/lib.rs (~30), clans.js (~40), towns.js (~25), panels-land.js (moved out of panels.js, 593), feed.js, sounds.json, atlas.json, view.rs (~20), towns.mjs (~90), check-stage.mjs (~30), core/tests/towns.rs (~80), clans.md and architecture.md (three lines), engine/CLAUDE.md, judge.md.

title: Towns that form and feed
why: Open 4, New 1, Miss 3, Reach 2. The home rule is small and the spec step's sketch shows it forms towns. What it leaves is the work: starving at three times main's, settled farmers hopping between their fields and the market, and 37% more turn. Eleven bounds, some pulling against each other (towns forming against towns feeding, crowds against the bench), judged only on the retro maps, and the rules run every turn. Opus low on the canvas rung. I expect it to build the rule, measure what build-1's exclusive gathering already fixed, find who starves, and change one or two rules, in eight to twelve sweeps. About 6 files, 250 lines: homes.rs (~80), clans.rs (~20), data.rs (TOWN numbers), fields.rs perhaps, core/tests/towns.rs (~100), cli/tests/save.rs pins, canvas.md.

twin.why: A rung above: does a canvas whose hard bound (towns feed) is a rule to find, not a number to tune, pay for more thinking? I expect Opus low to build the rule, tune the margin and the radius, and meet the forming, walking and scale bounds, with the starving bound near the line or an ask. I expect Opus medium to look harder at who starves round a town and change the rule that squeezes them, meeting bound 7 with room, in fewer sweeps. Both write canvas.md from the same seven maps, the same no-towns control and the same bench beside main, so the pick reads them side by side.

title: Review the piece
why: A rule change at the engine's centre: who lives where, who gathers what, and a turn's cost. The goal is judged on the retro maps against a control and in play, and every later M4 piece stands on it: Opus medium.
